catalog.chrome: Google Chrome web browser. Uses one process per tab, extension and GPU task.
catalog.webview2: Embedded browser engine used by other Windows apps to display web content.
catalog.safari: Safari web browser and WebKit page renderers.
catalog.vscode: Visual Studio Code editor, including its extension host and language servers.
catalog.cursor: Cursor AI code editor (VS Code based).
catalog.visualstudio: Microsoft Visual Studio IDE and its build/background services.
catalog.jetbrains: JetBrains IDE (IntelliJ, PyCharm, WebStorm…). Indexing can use lots of CPU and RAM.
catalog.docker: Docker Desktop and its container engine.
catalog.vmmem: Memory and CPU of the WSL2 / Hyper-V virtual machine (often Docker). Ending it shuts the VM down.
catalog.ollama: Ollama local AI model runner. Large models use a lot of RAM and GPU.
catalog.steam: Steam game store, launcher and its embedded web views.
catalog.riot: Riot Games client and Vanguard anti-cheat.
catalog.nvidia: NVIDIA driver services, overlay and recording tools.
catalog.adobecc: Adobe Creative Cloud background sync, licensing and update services.
catalog.figma: Figma design tool and its local font agent.
catalog.gdrive: Google Drive for desktop file sync.
catalog.svchost: Windows service host: runs one or more system services. Stop the service, not the host.
catalog.explorer: Windows desktop, taskbar and File Explorer. Ending it hides the taskbar until it restarts.
catalog.dwm: Desktop Window Manager: draws every window on screen.
catalog.searchindexer: File search indexer. Heavy CPU/disk use is temporary while it catalogues new files.
catalog.defender: Antivirus real-time protection. Protected by the OS.
catalog.wmiprvse: WMI provider host: answers system queries from other programs (monitoring tools, drivers).
catalog.tiworker: Windows Update installer. Ending it can interrupt an update in progress.
catalog.runtimebroker: Checks permissions for Windows Store apps.
catalog.windowserver: macOS display server: draws every window on screen.
catalog.launchd: macOS init system: starts and supervises every other process.
catalog.systemd: Linux init system and service manager.
catalog.displayserver: Linux display server or desktop shell.

user-temp.title: Temporary files & user caches
user-temp.effect: Deletes temporary files, crash reports and thumbnail/shader caches. Apps recreate them when needed; the first launch of some games or apps may be a little slower. Files currently in use are skipped.

system-temp.title: System temporary files
system-temp.effect: Deletes system-wide temporary files and old error reports. Your documents are not affected; files in use are skipped. Needs administrator rights.

update-cache.title: Update download cache
update-cache.effect: Deletes already-downloaded update installers. Installed updates are NOT removed; if an update is still pending, the system will download it again.

recycle-bin.title: Recycle Bin / Trash
recycle-bin.effect: PERMANENTLY deletes everything in the recycle bin. This cannot be undone and the files cannot be recovered.

dns-cache.title: DNS cache
dns-cache.effect: Flushes cached domain-name lookups. Helps when a site fails to load after a network change. No downside: the next visits simply resolve names again.

dev-caches.title: Package manager caches (npm, Yarn, pip)
dev-caches.effect: Deletes downloaded package caches. Your projects are untouched, but the next install will download packages again (slower and needs internet).

browser-cache.title: Cache
browser-cache.effect: Deletes images, scripts and files saved from websites. Pages load a little slower the first time. You stay signed in and passwords are kept.

browser-history.title: Browsing history
browser-history.effect: Deletes visited pages, address-bar suggestions, most-visited tiles and the tabs saved for "restore session". Cannot be undone. Bookmarks and passwords are kept.

browser-cookies.title: Cookies & sign-ins
browser-cookies.effect: Signs you out of EVERY website (email, social networks, banking) and erases site preferences. You will need to sign in again and may have to repeat two-step verification.
